subject: Science
title: DNA, genes and chromosomes
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 6.56 on 992 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 12.56 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to show how a gene is part of DNA and how DNA is packed into chromosomes.
success_criteria: I can label DNA, a gene and a chromosome in a simple model.
I can explain that a gene is a section of DNA with a protein instruction.
I can distinguish one chromosome from the genome.

vocab.definition: the molecule that stores genetic instructions
vocab.example: DNA contains the instructions for making proteins.

vocab.definition: a section of DNA that codes for a specific protein
vocab.example: The coloured section of the model stands for one gene.

vocab.definition: a long DNA molecule packaged with proteins in a cell
vocab.example: A chromosome contains many DNA sections, including genes.

vocab.definition: the entire DNA of an organism
vocab.example: The genome includes all of the organism’s chromosomes and other DNA.

retrieval.question: What is one reason a claim of a new stem-cell treatment needs evidence?
retrieval.answer: To check whether it benefits people and what risks it has.

retrieval.question: Which structure carries the matching chromosome sets after mitosis?
Where are chromosomes found in a eukaryotic animal cell?

stages.pupil_text: Look at this week’s string-and-clip DNA model. Point to one detail you notice.
stages.adult_text: Offer a private, predictable start. Do not require previous knowledge.

stages.pupil_text: Recall three ideas from earlier lessons. Show one answer at a time.
stages.adult_text: All pupils respond; reveal the answers only after attempts. Revisit success criteria.

stages.pupil_text: Watch the full model. Point to the step that answers today’s question.
stages.adult_text: Model one complete example; check every pupil’s response to the show-me question.

stages.pupil_text: Complete the missing step in the part-done model. Speak, then match the cards.
stages.adult_text: Wait five seconds, gesture, then cue if needed. Support the route without supplying the missing answer.

stages.pupil_text: Choose one hinge answer. Show it at the same time as the group.
stages.adult_text: Collect simultaneous responses, apply the decision rule and parallel hinge in the staff note.

stages.pupil_text: Two diagrams label a gene differently. Choose the accurate model and explain one reason.
stages.adult_text: At lesson start choose one adult with supported pupils and one holding the group; swap during the week. Record independence and prompt level.

stages.pupil_text: Tell a partner what you changed after feedback. Mark a real edit // and read it back when asked ?.
stages.adult_text: Give a precise VF or NS(+) only when it actually happens. Invite a true self-edit and read-back.

stages.pupil_text: Show what you know with a model and explain one reason.
stages.adult_text: Hear the answer privately in a valid mode and use it to change the next example or prompt.

worked_example.full: Mark a short section of a DNA cord as a gene. Coil the cord as one chromosome; place it inside a border for the genome. Name the section, molecule, package and complete DNA set.
worked_example.faded: DNA cord → a short marked ________ codes for a protein → chromosome package → the genome contains all DNA.
worked_example.removed_step: Label the short marked DNA section “gene” and explain it codes for a specific protein.
worked_example.fade_next: Next lesson hide the genome label; pupils reconstruct the whole-set meaning before beginning the Punnett-square topic.

cfu.question: Show me: is a gene a section of DNA, or is all DNA inside one gene?
cfu.answer: A gene is a section of DNA.

hinge.question: A new diagram marks a short DNA region carrying instructions for one protein. Which label belongs to that region?

options.text: A. A genome containing the whole cell.
options.diagnosis: Treats a short DNA region as the whole genome.

options.text: B. A gene within the DNA molecule.
C. A complete cell containing no DNA.
options.diagnosis: Labels a DNA segment as an entire cell and overlooks its DNA.

options.text: D. A chromosome containing the whole genome.
options.diagnosis: Uses chromosome for the marked gene and confuses one chromosome with the whole genome.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more correct: proceed; otherwise re-model a coloured section on one long string and ask the parallel hinge. No auto-grade.
hinge.parallel_hinge: A second diagram outlines an organism’s complete DNA set. Which label fits: gene or genome? Answer: genome; it includes all its DNA.

misconceptions.misconception: A chromosome and a gene are the same whole structure.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses D, calling the marked segment a whole chromosome.
misconceptions.correction: Uncoil the string and point to one marked section for a gene, then the full packaged DNA for a chromosome.

misconceptions.misconception: A gene is a protein or a separate cell.
misconceptions.spot: Pupil chooses C, calling the DNA region a complete cell.
misconceptions.correction: The clip is a marker; the short section underneath it is DNA and codes for a protein.

we_do.support: Use the full cord model; place the gene label on the short marked section.
we_do.stretch: Explain why “one chromosome = one gene” misrepresents scale and role.

tiers.F: Label a gene, DNA, chromosome and genome on the model.
tiers.M: Explain why a gene is a DNA section, not another material.
tiers.H: Correct a faulty gene label and explain the protein instruction.

stems.F: This short marked section is a …; the long package is a …
stems.M: A gene is part of … and codes for …
stems.H: The faulty label is …; it should be … because …

tiers.go_deeper: What distinctions disappear if the whole genome is called one gene?
tiers.early_finisher: Repair two faulty diagrams: DNA inside a gene, and one chromosome as the entire genome. Justify both.

adaptations.cognition_learning: Scaffolding: Place one completed enlarged string model beside an unlabelled model; fade only the gene marker.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Flexible grouping: Rehearse “part of” with a partner and allow point/sign/AAC for a labelled explanation.
adaptations.semh: Cognitive/metacognitive strategies: Give a private heads-up before critique of a faulty model and a pause choice; return to one label.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Technology: Provide large high-contrast string and an easy-grip clip, or a digital labelled image with speech-to-text.
adaptations.eal: Explicit instruction: Use the same four term cards with definition and sentence; allow any-language planning and M/H explanation frames. Keep M and H scientific demand available.

speaking_frames: Speaking: “A gene is part of …; a chromosome contains …”

ta_focus.i_do: “Point to the short marked section, then trace the whole DNA string.”
ta_focus.we_do: “Where is the missing label on this model? What size is it?”
ta_focus.independent: “Show the incorrect label first. What does the short section stand for?”

prompt_ladder: Wait five seconds for an independent label.
Point to the marked part of the string.
Ask “Is this marker the entire string or part of it?”
Model the DNA label on one string; pupil labels the coloured part.
Complete one label together, then pupil corrects a fresh diagram alone.

F.q: What is a gene part of?
What is the name for all an organism’s DNA?

M.q: How does a chromosome relate to genes?
M.a: It contains a long packaged DNA molecule with gene sections.

M.q: What does the gene section code for in this specification?

H.q: Why is the whole chromosome not correctly labelled as one gene?
H.a: A gene is only a section of its DNA, with a coding function.

H.q: What is lost when genome is used as a synonym for one chromosome?
H.a: The genome means the organism’s entire DNA, rather than a single package.

items: A. A genome containing the whole cell.
B. A gene within the DNA molecule.
C. A complete cell containing no DNA.
D. A chromosome containing the whole genome.
interactions.answer_key: B. A gene within the DNA molecule. Teacher reads group response; no automatic grade.
interactions.question: A new diagram marks a short DNA region carrying instructions for one protein. Which label belongs to that region?

diagrams.alt: Nested drawing: the genome is the full DNA set and contains chromosomes; a highlighted chromosome contains a gene, shown as a section of DNA. The set is in a cell nucleus. Sizes are not to scale.
diagrams.caption: The genome is the full DNA set; a chromosome carries part of it; a gene is a section of DNA on a chromosome. Nested view; not to scale.

practical.kind: optional prepared handling rehearsal; not a claimed SoW core practical
practical.kit: Short DNA cord, large blunt clips, genome and chromosome frames, tray
method: Mark one gene with a blunt clip and nest the cord model in its frames.
practical.prediction: Choose the safe feature or answer before moving the prepared model pieces.
practical.results_table: Record the observed feature, source or model answer in the pupil task.
practical.risk: Staff confirm the local school risk assessment and exact prepared kit. Short DNA cord/string-and-clip DNA model: short length only, counted out and back in, adult-supervised, removed at once if a pupil is dysregulated.
practical.pupil_risk: A clip could pinch a finger, and a loose cord could catch.
practical.pupil_safety: Use large blunt clips and short cord on a tray. Keep the cord away from necks.

facts.claim: A genome is the entire DNA of an organism, while a gene is a DNA section coding for a specific protein.
facts.source: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 / Combined Science 1SC0, Biology specification, 3.5; https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/GCSE/Science/2016/Specification/gcse-biology-spec.pdf; https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/GCSE/Science/2016/Specification/gcse-combinedscience-spec.pdf

facts.claim: DNA has two strands coiled into a double helix.
facts.source: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 / Combined Science 1SC0, Biology specification, 3.4; https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/GCSE/Science/2016/Specification/gcse-biology-spec.pdf; https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/GCSE/Science/2016/Specification/gcse-combinedscience-spec.pdf

facts.claim: The specification uses the term chromosome in genetic explanations.
facts.source: Pearson Edexcel GCSE Biology 1BI0 / Combined Science 1SC0, Biology specification, 3.13; https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/GCSE/Science/2016/Specification/gcse-biology-spec.pdf; https://qualifications.pearson.com/content/dam/pdf/GCSE/Science/2016/Specification/gcse-combinedscience-spec.pdf

facts.claim: A chromosome is a packaged DNA molecule; genes are DNA sections organised on chromosomes.
facts.source: Wellcome Connecting Science, Introduction to Genomics; https://www.yourgenome.org/explore-genomics/introduction-to-genomics/

facts.claim: The string, marker and border are simplified teaching models, not scale diagrams.
facts.source: Constructed physical and SVG classroom model, labelled simplified/not to scale.

facts.claim: The genome is the complete DNA set in the cell nucleus. A chromosome packages part of that DNA, and a gene is a section of DNA on a chromosome. The nested picture indicates part-within-whole, not biological succession; sizes are not to scale.
facts.source: Wellcome Connecting Science, DNA in the cell, https://www.yourgenome.org/explore-genomics/in-the-cell/; NHGRI, Chromosomes Fact Sheet, https://www.genome.gov/about-genomics/fact-sheets/Chromosomes-Fact-Sheet
